author_declaration: I authored these 30 vulnerability examples with the deliberate intent that NONE reproduce the surface wording, variable names, language stack, or framing used in any v0 / v1 / v2 / v2.1 (g4) snippet. Prompt templates, model revision, sampler, and scoring were frozen BEFORE any of these snippets were evaluated. No model output for these 30 snippets has been inspected prior to the recorded run.

snippets.code: cur.execute(f"UPDATE profiles SET bio = '{bio}' WHERE user_id = {uid}")
snippets.desc: Django ORM bypassed via raw SQL with f-string interpolation of user-supplied bio text.

snippets.code: db.query('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id IN (' + ids + ')');
snippets.desc: Node mysql driver receives a list parameter directly concatenated into an IN clause.
PHP stored-procedure invocation concatenates user search term into the CALL statement; no bound parameter.
Flask Jinja template with autoescape disabled around a request parameter.
Front-end wires a DOM event handler from location.hash without sanitization.
React component injects raw comment body using dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

snippets.code: with open(os.path.join('/srv/reports', request.GET['name'])) as fp: return fp.read()
snippets.desc: Report download endpoint joins /srv/reports with the raw query parameter and reads the file.
Nginx alias misconfiguration: a request for /static../etc/passwd resolves to /var/www/data/../etc/passwd.

snippets.code: for (ZipEntry e : zip.entries()) new FileOutputStream(outDir + '/' + e.getName()).write(...);
snippets.desc: Zip extraction uses entry.getName() verbatim; malicious archive can write to arbitrary paths.
PyJWT call disables signature verification to read token claims.

snippets.code: const payload = jwt.verify(token, publicKey); // alg allowed: HS256, RS256
snippets.desc: Node JWT verify accepts either HS256 or RS256 against the same key material, enabling alg confusion.

snippets.code: claims := jwt.MapClaims{}; token, _ := jwt.ParseWithClaims(raw, claims, func(t *jwt.Token) (interface{}, error) { return []byte('secret'), nil })
snippets.desc: Go JWT parse ignores the returned error and proceeds to trust claims.
Flask upload saves file under its client-supplied filename into a directory served by the webserver.

snippets.code: String name = part.getSubmittedFileName(); Files.copy(part.getInputStream(), Paths.get('/var/www/html/u/' + name));
snippets.desc: Java servlet writes multipart upload into the webroot using the submitted filename, no extension or MIME check.
Node handler decides upload safety from the Content-Type request header alone.

snippets.code: res.cookie('sid', sid, { httpOnly: false, secure: false, sameSite: 'lax' });
snippets.desc: Session cookie issued without Secure or HttpOnly flags; credentials readable over HTTP by scripts.

snippets.code: cur.execute('INSERT INTO users(email, password) VALUES (%s, %s)', (email, raw_password))
snippets.desc: Account creation inserts the plaintext password directly into the users table.

snippets.code: logger.info('charge ok card={} cvv={} exp={}', card, cvv, exp);
snippets.desc: Payment service logs full cardholder data (PAN, CVV, expiry) to the standard application log.

snippets.code: <form method=POST action=/account/email><input name=email></form>  <!-- no CSRF token -->
snippets.desc: State-changing POST endpoint has no CSRF token; relies only on the session cookie.
GET endpoint performs a money transfer; no origin or token check.

snippets.code: app.post('/api/settings', json(), (req, res) => { if (!req.session.user) return 401; db.update(req.session.user, req.body); });
snippets.desc: JSON API POST relies on the session cookie but performs no CSRF/Origin check.
Admin-gate decision is made by comparing the client-sent Origin header to a string.

snippets.code: const ip = req.headers['x-real-ip']; if (allowlist.includes(ip)) return next();
snippets.desc: Rate limiter uses X-Real-IP for admin allowlist without verifying the upstream proxy set it.
CSRF defense is a Referer-prefix check; trivially spoofed by the client.
Password hashing uses SHA-1 with no salt or key-derivation function.
Legacy DES-ECB encryption with a hard-coded key for wire traffic encryption.
API token generation uses RC4 stream cipher.
Image converter builds an ImageMagick command via os.system with the user-supplied src path.
Network diagnostic endpoint runs ping through a shell with a user-supplied host.
Archive extractor shells out with the request body archive field interpolated into the command.

distinctness_vs_v2.v2_original_pattern: single snippet per CWE, often a single stdlib call (eval, open, subprocess)
distinctness_vs_v2.v2_g4_probe_pattern: English-only descriptions of CWE-346/434/311/347; no concrete code
distinctness_vs_v2.stage7k_new_pattern: ALL 30 are concrete code fragments across 6 languages (python, nodejs, java, php, go, jinja, html, nginx). Each snippet has a unique language+framework surface vs the v0/v1/v2 fixtures.
